Hamlet is a revenge tragedy set in Denmark. Prince Hamlet meets his father's ghost, who tells him he was murdered by his own brother Claudius. Claudius then took the throne and married Hamlet's mother, Gertrude [1]. Hamlet vows revenge and pretends to be mad while he tries to confirm Claudius's guilt. He stages a play that re-enacts the murder, and Claudius storms out, which Hamlet takes as proof [1].

Things go wrong from there. Hamlet accidentally kills Polonius, who was eavesdropping behind a curtain. That death and Hamlet's rejection drive Polonius's daughter Ophelia mad, and she drowns [1]. Her brother Laertes wants revenge, and Claudius sets up a fencing match with a poisoned sword and poisoned wine. Gertrude, Laertes, and Hamlet all die, but Hamlet kills Claudius before he does [1]. The play is really about delay, doubt, grief, and whether revenge can be justified.
